Collaborate

/kuh-LAB-uh-rayt/ — stress on second syllable · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To collaborate is to work together with one or more other people toward a shared goal.

Two rival labs collaborated to map the virus in record time.

Worked Example

When the two rival scientists discovered a common problem, they set aside their competition and collaborated on research, combining their unique expertise to achieve a breakthrough.

Collaborate emphasizes the active teamwork and willingness to work together despite differences toward a shared goal. You could say 'work together,' but collaborate is more precise because it implies genuine partnership, mutual contribution, and a united purpose.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

cooperate: To cooperate is to go along helpfully with what others need or ask — you follow the shared plan and do your part willingly. To collaborate goes further: collaborators do not just support a plan, they create the work together, merging their ideas into one shared result.

contribute: To contribute is to add your own piece — money, ideas, or effort — to something larger that others are building; you can contribute once and step away. To collaborate is to stay inside the work with others, shaping the shared result together from start to finish.

collude: To collude is to work together secretly on something dishonest or unfair — rivals fixing prices, students trading test answers. Collaborate shares the working-together core but is open and honest: people who collaborate announce their shared goal, while people who collude hide it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

compete: to work against others toward victory

hinder: to block or slow someone's efforts

Where it sits · how fully the work is shared — assist → coordinate → partner → collaborate

assist vs. collaborate: Assist is the weakest: to assist is just to lend a hand with someone else's task, while to collaborate is to share the work and the goal itself.

coordinate vs. collaborate: Coordinate is stronger than assist but weaker than collaborate — coordinating means lining up separate efforts so they don't collide, while collaborating means actually creating the work together.

partner vs. collaborate: Partner comes very close, but collaborate is the strongest: partners join forces in general, while people who collaborate merge their ideas and effort into one shared piece of work.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — col- (com-)

Prefix — col- (com-): together, with (Latin)

Root — labor

Root — labor: work (Latin)

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: verb-forming: to make or do (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Col- ('together') + labor ('work') + -ate (verb ending) literally spells out 'to work together' — which is precisely what people do when they collaborate on a shared goal.

Use the root in a new word: laboratory

Use the root in a new word: laboratory: A laboratory is literally a place set up for work — it grows from the same Latin root labor, 'work,' that makes collaborate mean 'to work together.'

Word Choice

neutral / formal

Collaborate is the precise word when two or more people actively work together on a shared creative goal, bringing their unique skills to one purpose. Use it when partnership and mutual creative effort are essential. For simpler helping or just organizing efforts together, the words 'assist' or 'coordinate' work fine.
